chunks: And from it, concerning the end of time:

That is a time wherein only a sleeping (inactive) believer would be safe; if he is present he is not recognized, and if he is absent he is not sought after. Those are the lamps of guidance and banners of night journeys. They do not spread calumnies nor divulge secrets, nor slander. They are those for whom Allah would open the doors of His mercy and keep off from them the hardships of His chastisement.

key_terms.الْبُذُرِ: Those who slander or speak ill of others
key_terms.الْمَسَايِيح: Those who spread calumnies or backbite
key_terms.نُوَمَةٍ: Sleeping or inactive, referring to being inconspicuous or low-profile

ai.seo_question: Who are the 'sleeping believers' in the end times according to Nahj al-Balagha?
ai.summary: In Shia eschatology, this passage highlights the virtue of 'hiddenness' (ghaybah) during times of tribulation, where true believers remain inconspicuous to avoid persecution, a concept deeply linked to the era of the Minor and Major Occultation of the Imams. These 'sleeping' faithful are characterized by their quiet piety and lack of ostentation, serving as the enduring lamps of guidance amidst societal chaos. Their modesty ensures divine protection, reflecting the Shia emphasis on inner spiritual integrity over public recognition in the end times.

en.sayed-ali-raza: [A part of the same sermon concerning future times :]

There would be a time wherein only a sleeping (inactive) believer would be safe (such that) if he is present he is not recognized but if he is absent he is not sought after. These are the lamps of guidance and banners of night journeys. They do not spread calumnies nor divulge secrets, nor slander. They are those for whom Allāh would open the doors of His mercy and keep off from them the hardships of His chastisement.
